english: Where did the cows go? Other men drove them off early in the morning. Did my father fight against them? He fought against them at the fence, and he died. Who will guard us now? You will guard us, my son. Now you are a man. I am small, and I am afraid. Your father trembled too, and he stood up.

english: Brother, how many men did they kill? They killed seven men and our uncle. And where are the women now? They drove off the women and the children with the livestock. Did they take our sister too? They took her too. I saw her weeping. Then let us follow them. We will follow them in the morning; on this day we lay our dead in the earth.

english: Uncle, will they come back? They will come at harvest time. Then let us build a great wall. A wall did not save my brother. What will save us? A waking man and swift horses. I will stay awake this night. Stay awake, and I will sleep.

english: Shepherd, where were you born? I was born in the mountains. My uncle was a chief. How did you become a servant? They overpowered us in battle and seized me. Now I guard the sheep of my own enemies. Do you long for your home? I long for it; at night I see it in a dream. May you return home, shepherd.

pie: gʰórdʰe moy gʷṓs kʷsépi ph₂sdʰí. ḱwónes h₁régʷesi bʰéwdʰete. gʷʰéntōr-kʷe stóygʰom mē widóyh₁t. h₁ésyo-kʷe h₁éḱwos h₁ím Hih₁kyéh₁t. pérkʷune h₁ím h₂ḱm̥néh₁ kl̥h₂dʰí. gʷówes moy gʷowsth₂óm wékʷsperoy gʷm̥yóyh₁ent.
english: Fence, guard my cattle at night. Dogs, be awake in the darkness. And may the slayer not find the path. And may his horse throw him. Perkunos, strike him with a stone. May my cows come to the stall in the evening.

english: Warriors carried off a shepherd's grandson at the river. His grandmother sought him for nine days. Then she arrived at their settlement. At the door she saw her grandson carrying water. She gave the master her silver. The master took it and let the boy go. Grandmother and grandson returned home, and she shed tears with joy.

english: Husband, wake up! The dogs have become restless. I hear hooves at the wall. Take the children and hide in the cow-stall. Will you fight alone? I will fight with my brothers. Run now, wife! Husband, may the gods guard you.

english: Stranger, have you seen my son? Men carried him off toward the mountains. I have not seen your son, woman. Yesterday I saw men driving cattle and a child. They were walking toward the river. Was the child trembling? It was not trembling; it was following the cattle. Then I will go to the river. Go quickly, mother, and may the gods guard you!

pie: nókʷtes me sḱéh₃ih₂h₁ ḱélete. ḱwónes dʰwóri th₂kéh₁yete. gʰóstipoteyes moy ssih₁ént. nu me stóygʰe h₂ewsér wédʰe. déh₂nu me wéǵʰe h₂éHsh₂m̥ moy h₁ludʰóyh₁m̥.
english: Nights, cover me with shadow. Dogs, be silent at the door. May my masters sleep. Path, now lead me toward the dawn. River, carry me; may I arrive at my hearth.

pie: deywós wérunos diwés km̥tá gʷah₂t.
english: The god Werunos came down from heaven.

english: Other men drove our cattle across the river. That night they ate up our oxen and drank the mead. We lay in the grass and heard their boast. Their king said: We are bolder than these herdsmen. Their women will grind our grain. We did not tremble. We grasped our spears and waited for the dawn. At dawn we seized our livestock.

pie: ǵŕ̥h₂enti polh₁úh₂ wóydth₂e. mógʰus moy gʷíh₃weti? gʷíh₃weti. wódr̥ dweh₂róy bʰr̥h₁wéni bʰéreti. kénketi? h₁ím stundénti? kénketi h₁ím-kʷe stundénti. h₁ésyo ḱḗr dʰr̥sú. nésētor? tód ne dedórḱh₂e. deywóns ǵʰuHéye.
english: Old woman, you know many things. Does my boy live? He lives. He carries water at a far spring. Is he hungry? Do they beat him? He is hungry, and they beat him. His heart is bold. Will he return home? I do not see that. Call upon the gods.

english: Friend, do you hear them laughing? I hear them. Their boast is great. Let us climb down in the darkness and take back the livestock. They are many, and we are few. Our dead brothers lie at the door. Shall we sit and weep, then? We will lay them in the earth; then we will take vengeance on the laughing men.

pie: dusméneses h₂yuHn̥ḱéh₂m h₁r̥h₁pyónt mréys-kʷe h₂nr̥bʰós h₁íh₂m̥ pr̥h₂ént. h₁ésyeh₂s bʰréh₂tēr h₁íh₂m̥ tríh₂ wétesh₂ h₂isḱét. nu dweh₂róm stégos h₁ludʰét. kaptéh₂ Hyudʰsmóybʰos médʰu h₂én ǵʰéwt. swéh₂m swésorm̥ ǵnéh₃t. h₁esh₂ṓy h₁ésyeh₂s kʷoynéh₂m kʷinéwt nésonto-kʷe.
english: Hostile men carried off a young girl and sold her to men of the sea. Her brother sought her for three years. Then he came to a far house. There a captive woman poured mead for the warriors. He recognized his own sister. He paid the master her ransom, and they returned home.

pie: póyḱe toy gʷówes m̥rih₁ént. h₂éǵroysu-kʷe toy mē h₂wr̥syéh₁t. stégos toy témHesos dʰégʷʰoyh₁t. wetsṓs-kʷe toy mē h₂uksih₁ént. h₁nómn̥ kʷis toy mē gʷr̥nHyéh₁t. ḱwónes-kʷe te h₂éweyes-kʷe h₁édih₁ent.
english: Enemy, may your cows die. And may it not rain on your fields. May your house burn in the darkness. And may your calves not grow up. May no one praise your name. And may dogs and birds eat you.

english: Warriors carried off a shepherd's young daughter. She ground their grain and wove wool. She grew old in their settlement. She nourished her master's grandsons. The master's boy asked her: Where is your village? She said: I do not remember its name. At night she was sad, and she sang the songs of her village.

pie: pótni h₂éh₂usom h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m-kʷe bʰéretām. póyḱōm wóyḱom h₁r̥sḱóh₂. mē h₁éys. moréyōnti te. dʰugh₂tḗr nos kaptéh₂. h₁ésyeh₂s kʷoynéh₂m kʷinéwoh₂. h₁yód h₂éh₂usom h₁áyontor h₁íh₂m̥-kʷe ne léh₁onti? nu deywṓs tód dérḱonti. nu gʷh₂dʰí diwéy-kʷe h₂mélǵos ǵʰudʰí.
english: Wife, bring gold and wool. I am going to the settlement of the enemies. Do not go! They will kill you. Our daughter is a captive. I will pay her ransom. And if they take the gold and do not let her go? Then the gods will see it. Go, then, and pour milk for Sky.

english: Dawn, daughter of Sky, hear me now. My daughter is a captive among others. Now shine for her and show the path. Free her, and lead her to me. I will give you milk and honey.

english: Mother, where are we? We are in the strangers' house. They burned your village and drove you here. And who are you? They carried me off too, from my own hearth. Now I grind grain for the mistress. Shall I see my mother again? I did not see my own. Shed tears now, young one; in the morning you will work.

english: Now I sit by the sea and look toward the dawn. There my sister waits for me. My wife is sad indeed at the hearth. I was a free man; I am a servant. Wind, carry my word across the sea.

english: The king wanted a son.

english: Mother, it is I, your boy! I have come home unharmed. My boy! For three summers I was sad. How did you flee? My masters were sleeping, and I fled in the night. Are you hungry, young one? Eat! I am hungry. Is my grandfather alive? He is alive; he is with the herd.

english: Chief, the enemies have seized my husband. Give them the ransom! What did they ask? They asked a hundred cows. A hundred cows! Then our children would go hungry. Then my husband will die among strangers. I do not want that. We will pay half the ransom. And if they do not take it? Then we will take him back with spears.

pie: mógʰew te h₂éyeri lm̥bʰént. nu te h₂éwibʰis ḱóm h₁l̥h₂ént. péh₃tlom toy h₁idʰé h₂susyéti. príHe te h₂éǵroysu h₂isḱóh₂. poh₂iménn̥s prḗḱsm̥ th₂kéh₁yonti-kʷe. kʷís te méǵʰye dṓm wédʰeti? lewbʰóyh₁ te h₂éti widóyh₁m̥.
english: Boy, they seized you in the morning. Then they drove you away with the sheep. Here your cup is dry. Dear one, I seek you in the fields. I asked the shepherds, and they are silent. Who will lead you home to me? May I see you again, beloved!

pie: h₃rḗǵs ǵr̥h₂n̥tés dʰugh₂térm̥ lémbʰt. sénos h₁ésmey h₂éh₂usom h₂r̥ǵn̥tóm-kʷe wédʰet. h₃rḗǵs téh₂ ne h₁émt sénom-kʷe h₂epó ǵʰéyt. sénos mréy h₁épi sédt dyḗm-kʷe ǵʰuHéyet. dyḗws h₁ím ḱléwt. móros Hyudʰsmóns gʷṓs-kʷe h₁néwn̥ dinóns moréyet. nu h₃rḗǵs dʰugh₂térm̥ léh₁t sénōy-kʷe déh₃ōr déh₃t.
english: A king seized the daughter of an old man. The old one brought him gold and silver. The king did not take them, and he drove the old one away. The old one sat down by the sea and called upon Sky. Sky heard him. For nine days a plague killed warriors and cattle. Then the king let the daughter go and gave gifts to the old one.

pie: gʷówes moy gʷowsth₂ṓd lelikʷḗr. wetsṓs kénkonti h₂mélǵos-kʷe ne h₁ésti. nu moy népotes Hrupyónti. dusméneses-kʷe nos h₂mélǵos píph₃onti. uksnṓm-kʷe nos mḗms h₁édn̥ti. pérkʷune h₁íns h₂ḱm̥néh₁ kl̥h₂dʰí.
english: My cows are gone from the stall. The calves are hungry, and there is no milk. Now my grandsons suffer. And the hostile ones drink our milk. And they eat the flesh of our bulls. Perkunos, strike them with a stone!

pie: h₃rēǵéy-ge h₂éh₂usom bʰérom. nu h₁ésmey h₂r̥ǵn̥tóm gʷṓs-kʷe dédeh₃m̥. déh₃ōr moy ne h₁áyto smḗyt wérteto-kʷe. dʰugh₂tḗr moy h₁ésyo stégesi téksti. nu h₂éh₂usom h₂éti wéǵʰoh₂. dyéw moy ph₂ter ḱéh₂dos dr̥ḱdʰí.
english: I did carry gold to the king. Then I offered him silver and cows. He did not take my gifts; he laughed and turned away. My daughter weaves in his house. Now I carry the gold back. Father Sky, look at my grief!
